preferred_refinement.mechanism: Use one fixed immutable private SQLite seed solely as an OS-managed lock anchor. Open read/write, issue only BEGIN IMMEDIATE and ROLLBACK for exclusion; never execute application SQL writes, journal-mode changes, schema updates, vacuum or checkpoint after publication. MAC approvals and phase evidence remain separate immutable files.
preferred_refinement.seed: A packaged fixed closed-schema8192-byte seed may be published create-only. The disposable seed observed here is not yet the admitted packaged seed. Bind canonical seed SHA256, exact bytes, schema/version, owner/type/mode and its actual inode in the issuer. Reject any journal/WAL/SHM or changed seed; this protocol performs no SQL writes and has no journal recovery permission.
preferred_refinement.two_step_bootstrap: Avoid unresolved inode identities in a supposedly exact issuer preview: first show an exact seed/directory precursor plan and PREPARE RECONCILIATION-HOST <seed_plan_sha256> confirmation; publish only the fixed private seed and admitted0700 directories. Then actual directory/database identities exist. Prepare the complete private issuer with those identities and new key; show only exact size/digest and BIND RECONCILIATION-HOST <issuer_plan_sha256> confirmation, then private no-replace publication under the kernel lock. Cancellation after the precursor leaves only a recognizable inert seed, no issuer/key/grant. A later invocation may resume only after exact seed/type/owner/mode/schema/inode and namespace validation; unknown state refuses.
preferred_refinement.effect_bounds: No generic SQL/database capability or manually removed admission.lock. The typed reconciliation-host adapter owns only the fixed seed create, private read/write descriptor kernel lock and admitted issuer/approval/phase files. BEGIN IMMEDIATE holds until the synchronous guarded critical section ends; reject async callback, reentrancy and a second connection for the same host operation. Do not close another same-process connection while exclusion is held; serialize in-process admissions too.
preferred_refinement.recovery: Kernel exclusion is released by process death. Explicit Owner recovery still verifies the exact MAC-authenticated dead lease while holding the immutable anchor lock; it may quarantine/remove that lease safely because every lease publisher participates in this distinct kernel exclusion. No shared filesystem mutex is reaped.

preferred_refinement.posix_lock_descriptor_rule: Closing another raw descriptor for the same DB while SQLite holds its lock can drop POSIX advisory locks. Seed hash reads must precede opening the SQLite connection. During critical sections use exact closed SQL validation and metadata-only identity checks. Runtime/source-scan tests must catch readFileSync or other implicit open/close of the anchor while live. No second connection or closing alias is allowed. No-write planning is raw read-only and never opens SQLite writable or performs hot-journal recovery.
